summary: Best first deep dive. Has user-trade ingestion, Polymarket profile resolution, ClickHouse research schema, replication scoring, paper bot matching, maker fill calibration, and strategy reverse-engineering notes for BTC/ETH Up/Down wallets.
Most mature backtesting and execution-model reference. Useful for L2 replay, queue-position assumptions, latency/slippage/fee modeling, strategy boundaries, and BTC 5m sandbox plumbing.
Useful unified API reference for Polymarket Gamma/CLOB/Data APIs, WebSocket order books/trades, Python/TypeScript SDKs, and Binance feed normalization. Use read-only design ideas only.
Useful for smart-money and follow-wallet service shape, examples, dry-run flag, dashboard, risk limits, and SDK wrappers. Higher execution risk because private keys and trading examples are central.

Execution-heavy Rust toolkit with copy trading, BTC short-window arbitrage, OBI, market making, dry-run and safety layer claims. Reuse only concepts such as adapter boundaries, depth guards, and dry-run gates.

Best LP/market-making design reference. Has open-order monitoring, cancel/replace rules, reward-band pricing, anti-sniping filters, Telegram/Web controls, and Rust WebSocket-first rewrite. Not directly aligned with wallet/repricing.
Broad autonomous AI trading terminal across prediction markets, crypto, futures and wallets. Useful as a catalog of operational ideas, but too broad and execution-heavy for direct reuse.
Useful directory of prediction-market tools, analytics, alerts, APIs, smart-money trackers, and copy-trading services. Not code to reuse; good for future source discovery.
